key_insight: Twisting multilayer MoS2 moiré structures breaks symmetry and enhances tunable shift-current photocurrents by changing the wavefunction geometry.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests twist angle can be used as a practical design knob for engineering nonlinear photovoltaic responses in 2D solar-energy materials.
method: Built a Slater-Koster tight-binding model fitted to first-principles data for large moiré supercells.
Compared band structures and shift-current spectra against DFT and Wannier interpolation.
Analyzed shift distance to link twist-induced wavefunction changes with nonlinear conductivity.
evidence_signal: The model was validated by agreement with DFT/Wannier results near the band edges and by reproducing the main spectral features of the shift-current conductivity.
watch_item: Predictions depend on accurate parametrization and may be less reliable away from band edges or for twist/disorder effects not captured in the model.
paper_title: Twistronic control of shift current in multilayer moiré system
